haiku-low.q1: When the phone regains its connection, when the app comes to the foreground, and every 60 seconds while online.
haiku-low.q3: The server detects it by comparing the change's base version with the note's current version; a conflict is when they differ.
haiku-low.q4: The first write stays as note N at its new version. The second phone's body is saved as a new note titled with (conflict) at version 1.
haiku-low.q5: One change with the latest body, keeping the original base version and change ID. Several edits become one change.
haiku-low.q6: Processed changes records each change ID with its result. A retried ID returns the stored result without writing again.
haiku-low.q7: On the phone, as its cursor: the highest log sequence number fully applied. It is updated in the same local transaction that applies each page.
haiku-low.q8: The cursor did not move past the unfinished page, so the next pull restarts from the old cursor. Nothing is skipped, and reapplied entries are skipped by the version check.
haiku-low.q9: The server's reply says conflict. The phone replaces its local note with the server's current note, and the losing text arrives in the pull as the conflict note.
haiku-low.q10: When the server replies to it, whether accepted or conflict. The phone then removes it from the outbox.
haiku-low.q11: The download does not overwrite that note. The local copy stays until the server's reply for the unconfirmed change brings the current note.
haiku-low.q12: The sent change is not altered. The new edit becomes a second change that waits, with its base set by the first change's result.

sonnet.q1: The phone regaining its connection, the app coming to the foreground, and every 60 seconds while online. A trigger arriving during a sync makes it run once more when it ends.
sonnet.q3: The server. It compares the change's base version with the note's current version; if they are not equal, it is a conflict.
sonnet.q4: The first phone's write is accepted and the note goes to the next version (e.g. 3 to 4) with that phone's body. The second phone's body is stored as a new note titled with " (conflict)" at version 1. The original note is not changed by the second write. Each write adds a change log entry, and both change IDs are recorded as processed.
sonnet.q5: One change. The new body replaces the waiting change's body, keeping the original base version and change ID (as long as it has not been sent yet).
sonnet.q6: Each change has a unique change ID made on the phone. The server records processed change IDs with their results in the processed changes table. On a retry with the same ID it returns the stored result and does nothing else. This is done in one database transaction.
sonnet.q7: In a cursor on the phone, in its local SQLite. It holds the highest log sequence number fully applied. It is updated after each page, in the same local transaction that applies that page's entries, and set to the page's last sequence number. The server keeps no record of it.
sonnet.q8: The next pull starts from the old cursor, because the cursor only moves after a page is applied. Entries are not skipped, and entries applied again are skipped by the version check (entry version not newer than the local note).
sonnet.q9: The server's reply to the push says "conflict" and includes the current server note and the ID of the conflict note. The phone removes the change from the outbox and replaces its local note with that current server note. The losing text arrives as the conflict note in the following pull.
sonnet.q10: When the phone handles the server's reply, whether accepted or conflict. The reply may be a stored result on a retry. Until a reply arrives the change stays in the outbox, for example after a dropped connection.
sonnet.q11: The phone does not overwrite the note, because it still has a change in the outbox. The server's reply to that change brings the current note instead. (Entries whose version is not newer than the local note are also skipped.)
sonnet.q12: The sent change is never altered. The new edit becomes a second change that waits. If the first is accepted, the second takes the new version as its base. If the first is a conflict, the second keeps its old base, so it also conflicts and is saved as a conflict copy.
